subject: Canary A/B failure: promptset alpha v2 — coordination and rollback criteria
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@blueboxmedia.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: sudden drop in A/B for promptset alpha v2

Hi Nikhil,

We started the canary for promptset alpha v2 this morning and are seeing a significant hit on our intent-classification pass rate for the retail prompts slice — down from ~91% baseline to ~74% over the last 2000 requests. This is causing checkout assistant fallthroughs.

Can you confirm whether you rolled a model variant or prompt change on your side? We paused traffic but would like to re-open with clear rollback criteria.

Attaching the small sample we took and the failing examples.

Sam
Sam Lee
Platform Engineering — Bluebox Media
From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@blueboxmedia.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-12T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden drop in A/B for promptset alpha v2

Thanks Sam — I saw the sample and reproduced locally against promptset alpha v2 (the new promptpack + slight phrasing change). We shipped the promptpack at 03:00 PT as part of the canary rollout.

Quick status/update and ask:
- We confirm the v2 promptpack changed the system instruction that nudges policy-safe output; that appears to shift some disambiguation cases.
- Internal triage needed: product annotation review, eval owner validation, and an ops rollback plan if the A/B meets our rollback threshold.

Looping in Marissa and Ben to propose acceptance/rollback thresholds and an immediate short-term mitigation (route affected customers to pinned model v2026-04-28).

I attached: prompt_alpha_v2.jsonl (the promptpack we rolled) and a CSV with our locally computed eval deltas.

-Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
SRE — Inference Operations
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-12T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden drop in A/B for promptset alpha v2

Thanks all — I dug into the eval snapshot. High-level: the regression shows up primarily on retail 'price-ambiguity' prompts and some multi-turn examples where the model overprefers a safe fallback.

Suggested immediate plan (short, actionable):
1) Acceptance/rollback thresholds: if weighted acceptability drops >=8 percentage points on the customer-specified slice for 2 consecutive 10-minute windows, trigger rollback. (This mirrors prior gating rules but tuned for customer-sensitive slices.)
2) Mitigation: route Bluebox traffic back to pinned model v2026-04-28 and mark canary paused. Nikhil to implement routing toggle.
3) Product asks: Grace to run an accelerated annotation pass on the failing sample (we need 300 labeled pairs) and Karthik to run a targeted eval for the disambiguation prompts.
4) Communication: Ben to confirm notification to infra and CS with an ETA for rollback.

I'll own acceptance threshold and final signoff once we have the labeled 300-ex samples.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Evals & Quality
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@blueboxmedia.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-12T10:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden drop in A/B for promptset alpha v2

Actioning routing now. Plan: toggle Bluebox back to pinned v2026-04-28 in the next 7 minutes, surface a short outage note to their platform channel, and attach a link to the rollback_playbook.md.

ETA: routing toggle complete by 10:40 PT. I will post confirmation here and in the account Slack channel.

Attachment: rollback_playbook.md (stubbed; contains steps for canary pause, pin, and fallthrough monitoring).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Production Infra Lead
Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@blueboxmedia.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden drop in A/B for promptset alpha v2 — post-mortem actions

Follow-up after routing rollback and initial annotation pass:

Summary: routing rollback completed 2026-05-12 10:39 PT. Customer reports immediate reduction in fallthroughs. Our accelerated annotation produced 320 labeled example pairs; Karthik's targeted eval reproduces a 7.8pp delta on the retail slice (statistically significant at p<0.05).

Decisions and owners:
- Short-term: mark prompt_alpha_v2 as 'blocked' for wider rollout until we ship a targeted prompt tweak and re-run the canary. Owner: Marissa. Target date: 2026-05-20.
- Medium-term: add the retail disambiguation slice to our continuous eval suite and include the slice in canary prechecks. Owner: Karthik. Target: 2026-06-01.
- Ops: Ben to add an automated canary alarm for slice-level drops >=6pp so we have faster automated rollback. Target: 2026-05-18.
- Evals: Grace to produce a minimal re-run report (eval_delta_summary.csv) that includes both the 320 examples and aggregated telemetry for the affected window. Target: 2026-05-15.

Notes: Marissa — please capture the acceptance criteria text for this slice in the eval gating doc and link it to the promptpack PR. Also, add an item to the release checklist to run the targeted eval on any new promptpack push.

Thanks everyone — the cross-functional loop moved quickly and the customer is back to normal. We'll keep the blocked flag on v2 until the next validation pass.

- Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Evals & Quality
Redwood Inference
